design.normalization: Original canonical characters, punctuation, and whitespace are preserved through the end of the 50th word token; the suffix is discarded. No prose is reconstructed from tokens.

comparison_across_surface_pilots.observation: Controlling platform/register and then exact training/test word budgets does not rescue the character-based surface signal for Joel. The combined char-plus-word model again reproduces the word-only result rather than adding a reliable independent character-style signal.

interpretation.register_specific_conclusion: For the current Joel-vs-Dharma-control corpus and held-out discussion register, the paper-described surface SVM family is not sufficiently reliable to serve as the operational idiolect-retention calibration target. The char-only condition is at chance balanced accuracy and fails to identify any held-out Joel document. The remaining combined-model signal is indistinguishable from the lexical word-only condition in aggregate metrics and confusion pattern.
what_this_rules_out: Asymmetric TAFKA-vs-Dharma platform/register mismatch is not sufficient to explain the weak Joel character signal.
Unequal training document word mass is not sufficient to explain the weak Joel character signal.
what_this_does_not_rule_out: Surface SVM usefulness for other authors, larger corpora, other registers, other segmentation schemes, or other hyperparameters.
A deep authorship representation such as LUAR retaining useful Joel-specific signal.
Interpretable content-light/function-word controls detecting stable stylistic differences that this high-dimensional char model misses.
interpretation.next_test: Deprioritize surface SVM as the calibration target. Implement an isolated LUAR mean-profile nearest-neighbor lane on the same leakage-safe matched corpus, alongside content-light/function-word and word-order-shuffle controls. MiniLM remains a semantic/topic confound monitor rather than an authorship metric.
